messages:
neha: Quick sync — I'm re-evaluating the control plane network binding model for private/VPC customers. Current idea: per-AZ gateway binding (one connector per AZ subnet) vs a single regional endpoint behind Anycast. Pros/cons below, want quick takes.

matt: per-AZ feels nicer for egress/locality, reduces cross-AZ data transfer. but increases # of connectors and certificates.

liam: +1 to locality. also reduces tail latency when AZ hiccups, no cross-AZ failover needed. downside: routing and cert management ops multiply.

neha: exact. operational concerns: cert churn, rollout complexity, and how we expose that to customers (do they see N endpoints or a single VIP?).

sara: If we expose multiple endpoints we surface drift to customers. I'd rather present a single regional DNS and handle binding in control plane. internal topology can be per-AZ.

matt: that works if we can guarantee sticky routing -> same AZ as source to avoid cross-AZ egress. can we rely on the cloud LBs for that? some clouds don't give strong source-AZ affinity.

liam: we could make connectors advertise AZ-local IPs and have a lightweight L4 relay in-region. Alternatively, agent in customer VPC could pick the best AZ endpoint by probing `169.254.x.y` style metadata.

neha: probing is brittle. how about a hybrid: regional DNS with short TTL + a controlplane decision engine that returns an AZ-preferred IP per connection, plus a fallback anycast VIP. That keeps customer-facing name single but gives us per-AZ routing.

oliver: curious about implications for handoff: when customer subnets scale up/down, do we rebind connectors? rebinds = session churn which breaks long-lived gRPC streams.

neha: good point. plan: prefer connection draining and KV cache resync instead of immediate rebind. connectors should advertise a sticky token so we can attempt stream resume across ephemeral rebinds.

matt: stream resume idea is nice. we should add a simple backoff/delay policy so we don't rotate connections during transient autoscaling events.

liam: cost side: per-AZ connectors might increase controlplane instances by ~N_AZx factor. estimate: 3 AZs -> ~2.6x controlplane capacity for soft resources. NAT egress costs drop but infra spend rises. need a model.

neha: I'll run a back-of-envelope. but architecturally we should also consider a shrinkwrap connector: a tiny L4 forwarder that customers run in each AZ that does minimal auth+metric relay and keeps heavy lifting in our regional fleet. basically proxy vs full agent.

sara: that maps well to enterprise needs (minimal inbound surface). Would that proxy require KMS access? we want to avoid customer key material in our fleet.

neha: shrinkwrap idea: proxy holds TLS to customer CP only for transport, but mTLS to our regional controlplane using cloud-provided CA; no customer keys leave VPC. config sketch: 
```
connector:
  mode: shrinkwrap
  local_bind: 10.0.5.12:8443
  remote_controlplane: cp-usw-1.redwood.internal:443
  auth: ephemeral-token
```

oliver: Nice. security posture looks better. we still need to document cert rotation, tokens TTL and revocation.

infra-bot: Reminder: last private-controlplane cert rotation test passed 2026-03-10 15:22 UTC. No regressions in stream resumption test. :white_check_mark:

liam: ops question: how does observability change? if we have per-AZ connectors + shrinkwrap proxies, we need to correlate traces across proxy->regional->host. are we ok with adding connector-id headers everywhere?

matt: yes add X-Connector-ID and X-AZ metadata. also surface routing decisions in span attributes so we can debug mismatches (e.g., why traffic went to AZ-b instead of AZ-a).

sara: We should also add a policy for fallback when regional capacity is saturated: 1) prefer local AZ, 2) then same-region AZ, 3) then public-hosted (with opt-in for data egress). document this in the SLA doc.

neha: next steps: I'll draft an RFC that: outlines hybrid regional-DNS + per-AZ internal bindings, shrinkwrap connector mode, stream-resume token design, cert/token ttl recommendations, and observability headers. Targeting RFC draft by EOD Fri.

matt: thanks — ping infra and security for review early.

oliver: I'll prototype the shrinkwrap config and a tiny go forwarder this week, can share perf numbers.

neha: awesome — thanks all. tagging @matt @sara @liam for follow-ups. :rocket:
